newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawmakers slap blanket ban on tobacco adverts.
newsitem.headline: HK lawmakers slap blanket ban on tobacco adverts.

text.p: Hong Kong lawmakers have passed a tough law banning tobacco advertisements in public places, including the display of names of cigarette brands when corporate giants sponsor sports and cultural events.

The passage late on Tuesday of what was a controversial government bill bans all display of advertisements of tobacco products, while restaurants, banks, supermarkets and department stores will be required to designate no-smoking areas.
The bans will take effect two years from Friday, when the law will appear in public records, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
Cigarette advertising in newspapers and magazines will also be prohibited from the end of 1999, the spokesman said.
Legislators said the move was purely for health reasons.
"Well, it benefits the public, I hope it will cut down on the number of people likely to take up smoking," said Leong Che-hung, a legislator representing the medical profession.
"It also pushes the government into setting up a fund that supports sports and cultural activities," Leong said on a government-funded radio station.
Replying to threats from Hong Kong's tobacco industry to take action against such a blanket ban, Leong said he hoped the industry would be gracious.
"I think they should look at it that we are doing the society a favour and I do hope they will look at it as they are also doing society a favour," Leong said.

The move comes after cigarette makers in the United States admitted last week that tobacco was addictive, agreeing to pay US$368.5 billion over 25 years for damages and accepting extensive federal regulation over their products and advertising.
